summary_en: ROE 1.83% (target 5–6%), ROIC 1.99% (WACC ~2%), PBR 0.76x. Mid-term plan execution focused on commercial-facility, healthcare, and textiles segments; set to improve capital returns through margin expansion and growth visibility.
title_en: Progress Update on Capital-Cost and Stock-Price-Conscious Management
translation_en_brief: Daitobo disclosed progress on its capital-cost and stock-price-conscious management strategy announced in June 2024. The company reported FY3/26 results (year ended March 2026): ROE 1.83%, ROIC 1.99%, and PBR 0.76x. Management targets an equity cost of return of 5–6% and WACC of ~2%. While ROIC remains near the WACC target (1.99%), ROE fell significantly short of the 5–6% objective, continuing a multi-year trend. PBR remains below 1.0x, reflecting market skepticism about the company's growth profile stemming from its prior loss-making and no-dividend history. The company attributes the ROE shortfall partly to a capital structure heavily weighted toward long-term fixed borrowing. To improve capital returns, management is executing the mid-term plan "Jumping over the 130th," focusing on: (1) commercial facilities (operating flagship Santomoon Kakitakawa mall, expanding PM services, undertaking capex of ¥383M in FY3/25 against a 10-year plan of ~¥2.5B); (2) healthcare (posted first year-on-year profit growth in the health-business division in FY3/25; exploring M&A in underserved regions); and (3) textiles (returned to profitability for three consecutive periods; targeting domestic uniform and defense-related demand). The company commits to demonstrating improved profitability and growth prospects through transparent mid-term plan communication.
